# done — Completed work

**Append-only.** An entry is written when a slice of work closes, and is never edited afterwards. If
something recorded here later turns out to have been incomplete, that is a new entry, not a correction to
an old one — the record of what was believed finished, and when, is worth as much as the record of what
was.

**Chronological, oldest first.** New entries go at the bottom.

**What closes a slice.** Work is complete when its **exit condition** is met, not when the code is written.
Where [sequencing.md](./sequencing.md) states exit criteria for a stage, those are the condition, and the
entry says which of them were demonstrated and how. Where it does not, the entry states its own.

**Why this file exists separately.** Completed work will otherwise creep into either the decision journal
or the active-slice document, and it belongs in neither: [decisions.md](./decisions.md) is append-only but
records _why_, not _what shipped_, and [progress.md](./progress.md) is overwritten wholesale whenever the
active slice changes, so anything left there is lost on purpose. **When a slice closes, its outcome is
written here before `progress.md` is rewritten.** That ordering is the whole discipline.

## The entry format

```markdown
### What closed

**Date:** YYYY-MM-DD · **Commit:** `abc1234` · **Stage:** sequencing.md §x, or —

**Exit.** The condition that was met, and what demonstrated it.

**Notes.** Anything a later reader needs — what was deliberately left out, what it turned out to cost.
```

### Encrypted-store implementation phase one — write-session lifecycle

**Date:** 2026-09-08 · **Branch:** `codex/encrypted-store-contract-corrections` · **Stage:** L-1 component checkpoint, not L-1 closure

**Exit.** The agreed first implementation phase is complete. [writeSession.ts](../src/crdt/writeSession.ts)
acquires a shared slot permit before initialization, requires cleanup for initialization, invalidates
closed sessions and finished tasks, drains tracked work, clears caches and awaits native release.
Exclusive operations use the same lifecycle after the initiating writer closes; there is no upgrade,
timeout or stealing path. Failed cleanup disables writes and retains the permit. Reacquisition creates
fresh capabilities and reruns initialization.

**Evidence.** The [recorded browser execution](./storage-conformance-runs/2026-09-08-write-session.md)
passes 13 scenarios and detects five deliberate regressions, with zero harness or unexpected page errors.
It covers concurrent/frozen tab holders, task and session invalidation, detached work, partial initializer
failure, delayed/failed cleanup, queued cancellation, exclusive failure, renderer death, dedicated-worker
shutdown/termination and navigation. BFCache restoration was not observed. The full Vitest run passes
514 tests in 44 files; TypeScript, focused lint/format and the production build pass. `pnpm storage:session`
is included in `pnpm check`.

**Remaining.** This is the production lifecycle component with synthetic key-cache/write probes, exported
but not yet wired into the application. Mandatory-factor custody is the next phase; encrypted admission,
editor/receive integration and complete journal/generation/retirement composition follow. The C04 evidence
cell and its three existing debt pins were refreshed without changing obligations or paying any gate.
The independent L-2 record and earlier candidate outcomes remain unchanged. The component guide is

### Encrypted-store implementation phase four — synchronous encrypted journal

**Date:** 2026-09-08 · **Branch:** `codex/encrypted-store-contract-corrections` · **Stage:** L-1 component checkpoint, not L-1 closure

**Exit.** Phase three was committed as `468cbe2`. The [synchronous journal](./journal-store.md) now
attaches selected row-2 XChaCha20-Poly1305 bytes to mandatory-factor custody and the shared writer lifetime.
It reports success only after synchronous localStorage completion, refuses oversize/quota/unavailability,
authenticates full scoped snapshots, and preserves unreadable or unknown-generation entries. Recovery
captures journal before content to cover concurrent handoff. Flush commits captured bytes through the
real content allocator in bounded chunks and removes only matching entries after transaction completion.
Failed or changed cleanup retains the journal; no public caller-asserted receipt or clear API exists.

The existing RustCrypto WASM module gained authenticated opening, per-operation staged-buffer clearing
and permanent whole-memory disposal. The raw journal subkey and instance are cleared before the lifetime
permit releases. Selected journal vectors and locked cipher dependencies are unchanged. The shared store
name derivation was extracted without changing slot-index naming behavior. No editor/application wiring
or input-admission coordinator was added.

**Evidence.** The [recorded execution](./storage-conformance-runs/2026-09-08-journal.md) passes **17 cases /
93 assertions** and detects **six** mutants. It covers actual renderer death before flush and between
content completion/cleanup, real quota exhaustion, unreadable entries, concurrent handoff and late suffix,
actual freeze/resume/death with a cached journal key, close/disposal, and failure in a later flush chunk.
The content regression passes **13 cases / 58 assertions / five mutants**; custody passes **13 cases /
73 assertions / five mutants**, including its copied-profile controls. All three exit 0.

Full Vitest passes **554 tests / 48 files**. Type checking, focused lint/format, build/budget/origin checks,
WASM freshness and its **28 assertions**, published vectors and relevant contract/governance checks pass.
The WASM module is 8746 raw bytes; application initial JS remains **306.3 kB / 350.0 kB** gzipped. Desktop
append timings are a coarse-clock smoke observation, not payment of the low-end p95 or platform gate.
The literal full `pnpm check` chain, geometry and unchanged phase-one browser suite were not rerun.
`pnpm storage:journal` is included in the check chain.

**Remaining.** Ordered admission is next: prepare private input, force content on journal refusal, and
promote canonical state only after durable carrier completion. Actual editor/IME/undo/export/transport,
complete Local/Account startup/clear/migration, exact trim, generation/reference/receiver composition,
PRF and supported-platform/independent-review evidence remain owed. C11-prefixed journal-flush cases do

### Encrypted-store implementation phase five — ordered admission

**Date:** 2026-09-08 · **Branch:** `codex/encrypted-store-contract-corrections` · **Stage:** L-1 component checkpoint, not L-1 closure

**Exit.** Phase four was committed as `9e60c6a`. The [ordered admission owner](./ordered-admission.md)
now owns private canonical Yjs state and one FIFO over local intents, received updates and durability
barriers. Journal success promotes synchronously; refusal forces content before promotion. Queued intents
prepare only against the resulting accepted predecessor. Failed content retains exact prepared bytes and
retry remains on the content path. Receive validation precedes encrypted content completion and canonical
application. Recovery preserves unresolved structs/delete sets and refuses malformed persisted Yjs.

The component adds bounded byte/item reservations, explicit whole-suffix discard, retained pressure,
command-supplied slices, a 250 ms flush and `whenDurable()`. Canonical documents do not escape; snapshots
and accepted events are detached copies. Close immediately refuses input/publication, drains native work
and lets the existing lifecycle dispose custody. The owner is exported but not wired into the app.

**Evidence.** The [recorded browser execution](./storage-conformance-runs/2026-09-08-admission.md) passes
**15 cases / 64 assertions** and detects **six** mutants. Actual encrypted-storage schedules cover
refused predecessors, exact forced retry, receive-before-promotion, unresolved structs/deletes, slice
interruption, capacity, flush barriers/timer, malformed persisted Yjs, repair refusal and close/exclusion.
Renderer death demonstrates offline accepted-state/prefix recovery. An initially empty second tab
withholds a received update and dependent intent until its own content commit. Fixture projections and
publication inventories observe the real admission owner, not actual editor/transport implementations.

The journal regression passes **17 cases / 93 assertions / six mutants**. Full Vitest passes **574 tests /
49 files**, including 20 new admission tests for controlled failure and callback/ownership schedules.
Type checking, focused lint/format, build/budget/origin, vectors/AAD, WASM verification and relevant
contract/governance/traceability checks pass. Initial JS remains **306.3 kB / 350.0 kB** gzipped. The literal
full `pnpm check` chain, geometry and separate unchanged custody/content/phase-one browser suites were
not rerun. `pnpm storage:admission` is included in the check chain. The evidence records the corrected
native completion observer and the earlier development result without crediting its nonpassing baseline.

**Remaining.** Next is actual editor/command/IME/undo/export and receive/transport integration through the

## 2026-10-07 — Durable account session core (sessions/subscriptions phase 1)

Implemented opt-in schema 12 session ownership within the account database and a separate HTTP handler.
The current development adapter remains schema 11 and is unchanged. Fresh session-purpose WebAuthn
challenges bind the service, selected account and retry capability. The existing verifier authenticates
the assertion; the commit rechecks the account, credential, attempt and deadline. Historical receipts,
offline challenges and another account's assertion cannot mint a login. Session expiry is fixed at
30 days from the first successful sign-in commit; five-minute memory-only access is capped by that
deadline. Renewal and revoke-only secrets are independent, and ordinary session revocation retains
account/device credentials and other logins.

Exact lost-reply recovery uses an operator-key-derived, domain-separated AES-GCM issuance seal in the
same transaction as the session. Its nonce counter is reserved in a preceding committed transaction,
so aborted issuance burns a nonce. Acknowledgement/revocation retires the seal; expiry refuses replay
immediately and bounded maintenance removes old records. Key/pin changes or missing retained custody
fail opening. Schema 11 upgrade requires explicit opt-in, and the old adapter refuses schema 12. Live
upgrade tooling and restore tooling remain later integration/operations work.

The synchronous `withAccess` boundary checks session eligibility in the actual guarded transaction,
including revocation by another service owner. Review caught that a nested transaction failure could
otherwise roll back its caller; an entry guard and focused regression now prevent that. Existing
domain routes still need phase 3 integration with the boundary. The HTTP surface has origin/framing,
body, time, concurrency and rate bounds, structured refusal statuses and no private-token bypass.

Evidence: 25 new focused native checks pass (21 core, two SIGKILL/reopen, two HTTP), plus 13 existing
account-core and five existing development-runtime cases. TypeScript and scoped lint/format pass.
Initial HTTP checks hit sandbox loopback denial; approval review first failed due to reviewer capacity,
then an approved retry ran all seven HTTP/runtime cases successfully. No live data, server restart,

in [account-session-core.md](./account-session-core.md). Next is phase 2's client custody, ordinary

### 2026-10-09 — Lost-device recovery: separately authorized hosted reads

Added the private recovery-read route and bounded page protocol. Each request requires the retained
fresh passkey-authenticated attempt, a valid current recovery bootstrap and a signature from its

publishers removed by rotation, before returning accepted ciphertext and decision proofs. A final
transaction checks attempt cancellation/expiry, active account/credential, current authority and the
unchanged ledger. A changed head or incomplete ledger refuses. No ordinary device grant, membership
mutation, content write, network login or new schema is introduced.

Pages bind the entire request, nonce and signed accepted extent; 16 entries and 4 MiB are hard response
limits. A client verifier checks correlation, signature and forward progress. This is authenticated
ciphertext delivery, not yet complete cold semantic replay or editor installation. Concurrent appends
can change a later read extent; the later recovery commit must bind an exact verified cut.

### Own-stream receipt progression and incremental Account ledger experiment

**Date:** 2026-10-10 · **Commit:** signed `d5763346441ff98809442bb48b38ddd621516cd6` for own-stream
progress; incremental candidate is the working tree identified by the source/build hashes in its
packet · **Stage:** F-17 development repair; not release qualification

**Exit.** The first repair derives own receive progress from verified signed delivery receipts without
normal own-envelope download or duplicate self-inbound writes. It retains lost-reply, crash, legacy
receipt and cold-replay behavior. The operator then authorized incremental ledger validation: a
full physical census still gates an owner-local verified prefix, while eligible appends extend source,
spool, delivery and inbound state. Exact content replacement requires an independent full Yjs-state
equivalence check; positive coverage can survive it. Negative coverage is not cached. Proposed
precommit work never installs success. Context change, failed verification and late completion are
covered by invalidation and focused executed fault controls. Cold opening stays a full verification;
a periodic reference audit invalidates/reports any mismatch.

The [own-stream packet](./performance-experiments/2026-10-10-self-stream-progress/README.md) records
mixed later latency results, which motivated the next repair. The
[incremental packet](./performance-experiments/2026-10-10-incremental-account-ledger/README.md)
records predictions first, an early source/spool/delivery-only measurement, and a complete matched
0/520/1,220/2,220-edit pair. Both arms completed 2,320 edits. The fitted main-thread p50 slope fell
from 0.3799 to 0.0445 ms per prior edit (88.3%); deepest stable-text p95 fell from 5,071.9 to 613.3 ms.
Focused units, generated native edit/delete/compaction/reopen histories, commit-abort/lost-reply cases,
cross-generation differential replay, two packaged peer/history journeys, and three invalidation
fault controls pass. No full-reference disagreement was observed in those checks or the two normal
maintenance audits in the measured candidate.

**Notes.** The incremental product path remains **opt-in**, `VITE_ACCOUNT_LEDGER=incremental`.
Reference remains the default. Neither repair is deployed by this work; release validation stays
paused and F-17 stays open. Cold opening at 2,320 edits was 9.66 → 11.81 seconds, reopened post-GC
page heap 13.56 → 15.09 MiB, and candidate maintenance still reached 1.59 seconds with a full audit.
A synthetic 1 MiB coverage miss cost 13 ms p50. Added metadata/positive-cache budgets do not bound the
existing retained historical byte view. The next performance slice is the remaining physical census,
copying and admission-queue occupancy, with accepted-prefix byte retention and audit/cold costs

### Account consumer costs and immutable selection metadata

**Date:** 2026-10-10 · **Commit:** this entry's commit, based on signed `4500d9b6`; exact
measured/final source patches and hashes in the packet · **Stage:** F-17 development repair;
not release qualification

**Exit.** The next bounded performance slice implements lookup-table hex encoding, indexed byte
comparison, isolated Yjs validation without a random unused GUID, selected verified readbacks,
verified source-presence lookup, and Account reuse of owner-bound immutable selection metadata.
The uninterrupted profile identified selection-history copies as the largest avoidable consumer;
envelope selection was measured and was smaller. Account keeps its document fork, original source
capture, full post-admission verification, physical census, cold verifier and periodic reference
audit. No Local document handoff, global randomness override, historical-byte eviction or new
typing-burst batching policy was introduced.

The [consumer packet](./performance-experiments/2026-10-10-account-consumers/README.md) records
predictions first, fixed loads/transactions/authority/crypto counts per key and per position, an
uninterrupted 2,320-edit undo history, deep cold profiles, and two four-point comparisons in reverse
order. Against the signed baseline with its incremental path enabled, deep stable-text p95 improves
574 → 87 ms and 601 → 172 ms (85%/71%). Main-thread p50 at depth improves 184 → 124 and 186 → 129 ms;
its fitted history slope falls about 26%/17%. Cold opening improves 11.2–11.6 → 7.2–7.5 seconds,
reopened heap stays within about 1%, and each matched run executes two normal audits without a
mismatch. These are desktop observations on a small corpus, not phone estimates or an F-17 pass.
The faster path emits more positions at depth; total observed record-copy bytes rise, despite fewer
source decodes. Remaining cold reconstruction and maintenance costs are substantial.

**Verification and activation.** 73 focused unit tests, five audit-every native sync checks, four
current-key retry checks, the explicit reference override, TypeScript, targeted lint and the ordinary
packaged build pass. Packaged peer/history checks have both passes and failures: repeated ordinary
runs time out on post-maintenance delivery; other attempts stop during enrollment. Both candidate
journeys and baseline controls also pass with diagnostics. HTTP 429s and existing retry backoff are
plausible timing contributors, not an established explanation. Failures and diagnostic patches are
retained. The separate probe's profiler-detach/virtual-passkey defect was reproduced in isolation
and fixed; its failed final cold attempts are excluded from successful cold-open results.

**Default activation is held.** The major optimizations remain behind
`VITE_ACCOUNT_LEDGER=incremental`; the temporary proposed default was reverted. No public deployment
was made in this slice, and release validation remains paused. Next resolve the packaged
enrollment/delivery result, then reconsider activation. Accepted-prefix retention, repeated cold
verification, rows per typing burst and maintenance stalls remain open performance work. No other
